verdict.tagline: A confusing start masks a deep shooter, but technical barriers block entry.
for_you_if: you already navigate complex expansion systems
you have patience for unguided early hours
not_for_you_if: you play on Linux or Steam Deck
you expect a clear starting direction

distortion_flags.sentence: Approval rises as players move past initial technical roadblocks and onboarding friction.

cohorts.summary: New players hit immediate technical roadblocks with server connections and platform compatibility.

claims.claim: Reviewers experience server connection failures accompanied by the weasel error code.

citations.review_text: Downloaded and was excited to finally start playing. Unfortunatly i keep getting the weasel error code and wont let me onto the servers. Very sad for a game thats supposed to be great.
Great game. Couldn't get past the character choosing screen, though. Constantly showed a "weasel" error. Nothing in the troubleshooting guide Bungie provides was helpful.

claims.claim: This cohort reports that the game blocks Linux and Steam Deck support, with developers considering it a ban-worthy offense.

citations.review_text:
Excited to play with friends, only to find out that the developer is actively hostile to SteamOS, Steam Deck and Proton support. It seems the game was working fine on Linux until 2023 when Bungie decided this was no longer okay.

This is not an opinion, their FAQs talk about the fact they consider this cheating and it will result in a ban. Most developers who do not wish to put in the time to support Linux will simply advise it's a user beware, and put in the (extremely small) effort of shipping with a Linux Battleye integration, but I've never seen an actively hostile viewpoint.

Incredibly disappointing and a decision that will be looked back on very poorly in the future I'm sure.

cohorts.summary: Early progression is hindered by high expansion costs and an unguided onboarding experience.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the onboarding and new player experience as confusing and unguided after the initial quests, leaving players without clear direction on what to do next.

citations.review_text:
Best gunplay in any shooter, period. The loot grind is addictive, the builds are super fun to experiment with, and the raids/dungeons are incredible if you have a group. It can be a bit confusing for new players at first, and the DLCs add up in price, but once you get into the flow, it’s easily one of the most satisfying games to play. Worth a shot.


Pros:
> Crisp, unmatched gunplay and abilities
> Deep buildcrafting and loot chase
> Amazing music, art direction, and raids


Cons:

> Rough onboarding experience for beginners
> Expensive if you want all the expansions

I'm really enjoying Destiny 2, I think the freedom and variety in content is awesome and the guns feel really nice to use. The classes and subclasses I think offer playstyles suitable for pretty much anyone, I like how some guns are clearly better than others but none are unviable, I wish they made more of the DLC content available for free but even then the other content makes up for it. However, I don't like that after the new light quests the game offers no additional guidance, and gives you access to everything immediately, which can feel very intimidating. I shouldn't have to search up guides and such just to figure out what I should be doing. But even so, I was able to figure it out, farm for some nice armor, and figure out my first actual build. Overall very good game so far solid 8/10.

I've come back after a 16 month layoff from the game & I have to say it's in a miles better state than when I left it. It can be a tad overwhelming though if you're a returning player with the amount of stuff the game throws at you right off the rip & as it's been said before, the onboarding for new players is still rubbish. All in all though, I would recommend it.

As a brand new player, this game is a chaotic, unintuitive mess. After you finish the brief tutorial in the starting area and arrive at the main hub, the game completely abandons you. Because bungie deleted the original base campaign years ago, there is zero natural narrative momentum, no chronological story path, and no clear direction on where to go next.

Instead, the map floods your screen with an ambiguous web of planetary icons, out of order expansion intros, locked activities, and arbitrary prerequisites. The game does virtually nothing to explain the lore, the chronological order of surviving campaigns, or how to properly work your way up to endgame content like Dungeons and Raids.

If a game requires you to close the application and spend hours studying youtube guides and wikis just to figure out what to play next, its onboarding design is fundamentally broken. The graphics are good and gunplay is fantastic, but for a newcomer, the user interface and new player experience are completely disrespectful of your time.

Sure, you can run around like a headless chicken clearing random planet quests with zero context, but for some, including me, that is a waste of time. Defenders will claim this confusion is inevitable for a long running mmo, but mmos like ff14, wow, swtor etc prove otherwise, they preserve a clear, linear path from day one to the endgame, no matter how late you start or how many expansions they added. Destiny 2 doesn't.

Avoid this if you want a coherent story experience that actually respects your time.

tried it again after quite some time, as i used to play it a bunch on ps4 back in red war and stuff. and finally got it on pc to play again, and honestly?

i can't recommend it. it's so boring now, and they've taken out a lot of the stuff you could do on the side, like i remember collecting materials and turning them in for reputation and stuff. and for what? because with that at least you'd have something that you could do on the side. what do they expect you to do now? collect exotics, and do the same mission over and over and over again for xp for some mediocre-at-best battle pass.

maybe im crazy but i missed when the game was actually good and not just cash-grab slop with half-assed campaigns locked behind a 10-20 dollar price tag. it's a shadow of it's former self.

The game reminds me of Warframe. I still don't understand a lot of things, but the gameplay feels incredibly well-made and the environments are amazing. I'm just waiting for the DLCs to get cheaper so I can buy them and enjoy the complete experience.

claims.claim: Reviewers state that the new player onboarding experience is confusing, unguided, and overwhelming.

citations.review_text: Once you get into it, and believe me when I say the onboarding experience won't be kind to you, it might just become your favourite game of all time. Really great stuff

Game: Free
To actually play it: $200 in DLCs
New Light experience: pure confusion, everyone speaking alien, you getting one-shot
I love it. 10/10

As someone that has played D1 and D2 and practically grew up with the game. I will say that this is one of the games that will forever be in my heart. Despite the up and downs. The new player experience is def overwhelming and seems like a lot and the MTX will always be well....MTX. But the world, lore, and gameplay/gunplay will always be up there.

I do recommend the game if you can get past the bad and underwhelming parts.

(Just a sidenote. I hope Bungie give D2 the love and care it deserves with it being supported again. Their "last" update was a banger and it showed they can do it.)
I've been having a great time playing this game. It is very difficult to get into and learn how it works, I highly recommend playing with someone who is more familiar.

single_points.text: One reviewer says the game's UI is awful, map directions are scarce, and it is extremely hard to level armor without knowing what you are doing.

citation.review_text: This game's UI is awful. The actual content is interesting and unique which I enjoy, but I never know where I'm supposed to go for anything. The directions for maps are few and far between. Its also extremely hard to level your armor if you do not know what you are doing. I  wish this game was more enjoyable as a newer player but, it is simply not. Cosmetics are beautiful and I can see that there is a good story but the User Interface really makes me turn away from this game.
